sentences.text: This bail application has been moved on behalf of the petitioner(s) in FIR No. 411/2017, P.S. Udyog Nagar, Kota registered for the offence under Sections 420, 272, 273 IPC and Section 102, 103, 104 of Trade Mark Act and Section 63 of the Copy Right Act as also Section 51 of Food Safety and Standard Act.
The allegations against the accused-petitioner are that he was apprehended while forgedly preparing 35 packets of 1 kg. each of Saras Ghee.

The case has been registered for the offence under Sections 420, 272, 273 IPC and Sections 102, 103, 104 of (2 of 3) [CRLMB-12543/2017] Trade Mark Act and Section 63 of the Copy Right Act as also Section 51 of Food Safety and Standard Act.
Learned counsel for the accused-petitioner submits that the offences alleged against the petitioner cannot be substantiated looking to the provisions of the relevant Acts.
The allegation for the offence under Section 63 of the Copy Right Act is not made out in view of the provisions contained in Sections 13 & 14 of the said Act.
Likewise, provisions of sub-Section (4) of Section 115 of the Trade Mark Act has not been complied with as the case has not been registered by the officer of the rank of DSP or equivalent.
Further, the opinion of the Registrar as required under proviso to sub-Section 4 of Section 115 of the Trade Mark Act has also not been obtained.
He further submits that Section 51 of the Food Safety & Standard Act,2006 provides only pecuniary penalty up to Rs.5,00,000/- and no sentence, therefore, has been prescribed.
For offences under Sections 272 & 273 IPC, he further submits that three offences are only bailable.
He further argued that there is no allegation that the accused-petitioner committed the offence under Section 420 IPC by deceiving any person to purchase the allegedly forged Saras Ghee.
He also submits that the accused- petitioner is in custody since 26.08.2017.

] Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case but taking into consideration the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it just and proper to enlarge the petitioner(s) on bail.
Consequently, the bail application filed by him under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

(DEEPAK MAHESHWARI),J.
